title: MAR: Metacognitive Agentic Reasoning for Multimodal Fake News Detection

problem.claim: Multimodal fake news combining text and images is increasingly prevalent on social media.

gap.claim: Existing supervised small multimodal language models have limited knowledge scope and reasoning capability, degrade on novel content, and typically produce uninterpretable binary predictions.

contributions.claim: MAR integrates multi-agent metacognitive debate with external knowledge retrieval for multimodal fake news detection.
MAR uses Believer and Skeptic agents in a three-stage Draft–Self-Critique–Refine debate process.
MAR dynamically retrieves external knowledge through web and reverse image searches to improve factual reliability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance on two benchmarks and significantly better generalization and interpretability than existing methods.
The source code is reported as publicly available in the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal fake news is increasingly prevalent through social media dissemination.
Existing supervised approaches struggle with novel content and provide binary, uninterpretable predictions.
MAR combines multi-agent metacognitive debate with external knowledge retrieval.
Agents draft judgments, critique arguments, and refine conclusions using internal or external evidence.
The authors report improved benchmark performance, generalization, and interpretability, with code availability.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines structured self-critique and refinement with externally retrieved evidence.

interpretation.claim: Separating initial judgment from critique and revision may help make multimodal reasoning more robust and inspectable.

application.claim: For multimodal classification tasks, consider staged reasoning with explicit critique and evidence retrieval.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which component causes the reported improvements or how the approach performs under retrieval failure.

unknowns: Benchmark names, datasets, metrics, and experimental settings are unspecified.
The number and implementation details of agents are unspecified.
The external knowledge sources, retrieval quality, and failure cases are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
